display_name: Shafer Vineyards One Point Five, Napa Valley
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Shafer's One Point Five sources Cabernet Sauvignon from their hillside vineyards on the Stags Leap District's edge, where volcanic soils from the Mayacamas Mountains meet Napa Valley's alluvial valley floor. This blend of sites delivers blackcurrant depth with graphite edge and grippy tannins. At 15.3% ABV in recent vintages like 2022, it balances ripeness and structure.",
  "wine_summary": "Shafer Vineyards farms 55 acres across Napa Valley estates, focusing on hillside Cabernet that ages decades. One Point Five pulls from multiple blocks, including Hillside Select vines, to craft a Napa Cabernet that rivals single-vineyard bottlings without the premium price. The producer's dry-farming approach—vines sink roots deep into varied soils—forces concentration, yielding wines with blackcurrant core, dark chocolate layers, and tobacco notes that evolve over time.",
  "terroir_expression": "Alluvial Bale loam on the valley floor provides vigor for ripe black plum and cassis, while iron-rich Hambright volcanic soils in the western Mayacamas stress vines for graphite minerality and firm tannins. The narrow 30-mile valley's Mediterranean climate—cool bay fog mornings warming to 90°F afternoons—preserves acidity amid ripeness, translating to dark cherry lift cutting through dense fruit. Sedimentary Franciscan formations on eastern hills add subtle herbal cedar, distinguishing this from softer valley-floor Cabernets.",
  "vinification_summary": "Shafer ferments in small stainless lots with native yeast, then ages 28 months in French oak (50% new) to integrate vanilla and cedar without overpowering fruit. Native fermentation preserves site-driven purity, capturing blackcurrant vibrancy from volcanic blocks. Barrel selection mimics their Hillside Select rigor, ensuring structure for aging.",
  "food_pairing": "Nashville hot chicken: spice meets grippy tannins and graphite edge, blackcurrant fruit tempers heat. Ribeye with béarnaise: fat and herb sauce bind to firm structure, dark chocolate notes amplify umami. Lamb tagine with apricots: sweet-savory fruit echoes cassis ripeness, acidity slices through richness. Cheeseburger with aged cheddar: casual char pairs with tobacco depth, tannins grip beef proteins. Venison Wellington: fine-dining game leans into cedar and plum density.",
  "comparable_wines": "Opus One Napa Valley — shares hillside volcanic influence for graphite structure at similar ripeness. Spottswoode Cabernet Sauvignon — comparable alluvial-volcanic blend yielding cassis-driven intensity. Dominus Estate — Napa's Bordeaux blend analog with firm tannins and dark fruit evolution.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry Cabernet with grippy tannins and graphite minerality",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2022 from 2026-2035; earlier vintages like 2019 hit peak now through 2030. Store at 55°F, 70% humidity, away from light.",
  "value_assessment": "$125-$140 retail positions it against Spottswoode ($160+) and Opus One ($350). Shafer's hillside sourcing and 28-month oak match that quality tier. Buy for aging depth that outlasts price peers.",
  "market_position": "Napa collectors stock this on cellar racks for its Hillside Select lineage. High-end steakhouse lists feature it by the glass at $30 pours. Savvy retailers push to Cabernet enthusiasts seeking structure without trophy pricing.",
  "insider_take": "Skip if you chase plush, low-tannin Napa fruit bombs—this demands food and patience. Most overlook how volcanic blocks build graphite backbone that 10-year vintages reveal. Stock for venison dinners; it's built like Dominus at half the cost.",
  "aging_potential_years": 20,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 4,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 15,
  "sensory": {
    "acidity": 4,
